The Oxford comma, also known as the serial comma, refers to the use of a comma before the conjunction in a list when there are three or more items in that list. For example, in the phrase "I bought apples, oranges, and bananas," the comma before the "and" would be the Oxford comma.

Editors often debate the use of the Oxford comma due to its impact on clarity and style within certain contexts, particularly in legal and financial documents where precision is paramount.
